Draft upstream GitHub issues for the public tfp-photonics/treams repository, one per confirmed treams defect, each with a verified minimal reproducer. DRAFT ONLY: do not create, comment on, or edit any GitHub issue. I will review the drafts and post them myself.

Source of findings

Read docs/upstream-findings.md. It lists defects found by comparing against treams 0.4.5 at reference commit 1f5d0d6ebb007288f28bc9e16f6d266e8b55dc39. The linked tests in tests/ often contain exact parameters and upstream calls that are useful for building reproducers. An upstream source checkout may be at reference/treams.

Hard constraints

  • The issues must not mention treams-rs, Rust, a rewrite or port, a "native" implementation, AI or agents, or any private repository, file or test name. Each issue must stand on its own as an ordinary bug report from a treams user.
  • Reproducers use only public treams API plus numpy, scipy, and h5py or gmsh where the bug requires them. Each one prints the actual result and states the expected result with an independent justification: an analytic value, a physical invariant (identity, unitarity, energy conservation, invariance), SciPy, or a direct numerical check written inline. Keep them as short as possible.
  • Verify every reproducer against the LATEST upstream code, not just 0.4.5. Clone https://github.com/tfp-photonics/treams into your scratch directory and check whether main has moved past the pinned commit. Run reproducers in a clean environment with the latest PyPI release, e.g. uv run --no-project --with treams --with h5py python repro.py. If main differs from the release in relevant code, install from the main checkout as well. Drop any finding that no longer reproduces on current main, and record why.
  • Search existing issues, open and closed (gh issue list -R tfp-photonics/treams --state all --limit 200, plus gh search issues), for duplicates. #14 (skew-cell orders), #20 (evanescent cylindrical widths) and #27 (chiral sphere parity) are already reported, so skip them. Skip any other duplicate you find and name the existing issue.
  • Read-only GitHub access is fine. Never run gh issue create, gh issue comment, or any other mutating command.

Which findings to draft

  • Every row in "Behavioral defects", except the three already reported.
  • In "Numerical accuracy limitations", draft the ones that are genuine treams-side precision or documentation defects with a clear expected value. Likely candidates: near-axis spherical translation returning zero coefficients, the small-angle rotation rounding, axial complex-medium forbidden-mode leakage, the cylindrical Ewald automatic-split inaccuracy, the fractional Legendre docstring/behavior mismatch (lpmv says it delegates to SciPy but returns 0 for |m| > degree), and the SMatrices.cd docstring calling T+R contrast "absorption CD". Use your judgement.
  • Do NOT draft the following, which the document itself classifies as non-defects or non-treams issues: exact diffraction-pole regularization, the degree-6 EBCM cancellation floor, the SciPy subnormal Hankel bug, the companion-paper notebook, the thermal-radiation discrepancy, and the G/F normalization convention.
  • If a finding cannot be reproduced with a short public-API script, say so. Do not force it.

Style

Look at a few existing upstream issues (e.g. #14, #20, #27) and match their tone and length. Each issue has a specific, plain title and a body containing: one or two sentences on what is wrong, the reproducer in a ```python block, actual vs. expected output, the likely cause with a source reference (file and function, using a permalink to the current main commit where useful), and an environment line (treams version or commit, Python, numpy, scipy). Keep it concise, factual and non-judgmental, with no filler or boilerplate sections. Follow the user's writing guidance in [a private folder] (read what is there) where it applies to short technical prose.

Output

Write each draft to scratch: upstream-issues/NN-short-slug.md. The first line is # <title> and the rest is the exact issue body. Put the runnable reproducer beside it as NN-short-slug.py, together with the captured output from the latest release (and main, if different) as NN-short-slug.out.

Your final report to me should be a table with these columns: file, title, reproduced on latest release (y/n), reproduced on main (y/n), and duplicate/skip reason if any. Add a short list of findings you dropped and why, the upstream main commit and PyPI version you tested, and anything you are unsure about.

I've drafted 22 issues in .../scratchpad/upstream-issues/, each with its .md draft, runnable .py and captured .out. All reproduce on the latest release. Nothing was created, commented on or edited on GitHub; I only used read-only gh calls and a clone in the scratchpad.

Versions tested: PyPI treams 0.4.7 (tag v0.4.7 = 96abd7b) and upstream main 1f5d0d6, which is the same commit as your pinned reference. Main differs from 0.4.7 only in six docs and notebook files, and the installed Python sources are byte-identical to main, so I didn't build main separately. The "main" column means "same source". Environment: Python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.16.3, plus h5py 3.16.0 and gmsh 4.15.2 where needed.

Titles follow the upstream [BUG] prefix convention, and the bodies use the template headings without the checklist.

file title latest release main duplicate / skip
01-plane-wave-rotate-basis rotate on plane-wave arrays only rotates the output basis, and SMatrices.rotate raises AttributeError y y
02-gfield-ffield-attribute PhysicsArray.gfield and PhysicsArray.ffield raise TypeError y y
03-operator-attribute-rebinding Operator attributes are shared between instances, so a saved a.rotate acts on another object y y
04-mesh-spheres-surface-groups io.mesh_spheres puts the wrong surfaces in the physical surface groups when the model is not empty y y
05-save-hdf5-computation-without-mesh save_hdf5 raises NameError when computation has no mesh y y
06-lattice-sums-tiny-bloch-vector Lattice sums lose a term and then raise ZeroDivisionError for tiny nonzero Bloch vectors y y
07-dsumsw1d-shift-x-displacement lattice.dsumsw1d_shift treats a displacement along x as a displacement along the lattice axis y y
08-dsum1d-negative-half-cell lattice.dsumsw1d and dsumcw1d ignore the sign of a half-cell displacement y y
09-hdf5-embedding-chirality load_hdf5 ignores the embedding chirality written by save_hdf5 y y
10-save-hdf5-single-tmatrix save_hdf5 raises IndexError for a single TMatrix y y
11-hdf5-mode-positions load_hdf5 drops mode positions and cannot read T-matrices with several positions y y
12-chirality-density-interval chirality_density over a z interval: wrong for propagating waves, NaN for evanescent waves y y
13-ebcm-surface-element ebcm.qmat is missing a factor r(θ) in the surface element y y
14-plane-wave-complex-transverse-branch Spherical-wave expansion of a plane wave with complex transverse wave vector uses the wrong sin θ branch y y
15-plane-wave-basis-by-comp-slicing Slicing or combining a PlaneWaveBasisByComp resets the alignment to "xy" and drops lattice and kpar y y
16-near-axis-spherical-translation Spherical-wave translation coefficients lose accuracy and vanish for shifts close to the z axis y y
17-small-angle-rotation rotate and wignersmalld lose the first-order terms for small polar angles y y
18-axial-plane-wave-complex-medium Axial plane wave in a lossy medium expands into forbidden azimuthal orders y y
19-lsumcw1d-automatic-eta Automatic Ewald split in lsumcw1d is inaccurate for large k * a y y
20-lpmv-fractional-degree special.lpmv returns 0 for |m| > v with a non-integer degree y y
21-smatrices-cd-definition [DOC] SMatrices.cd: the second value is not the usual absorption CD y y
22-byunitvector-zx-alignment PlaneWaveBasisByComp.byunitvector does not handle alignment "zx" y y Not in your findings doc. I found it while drafting 15; drop it if you want to stay in scope.
(not drafted) Plane-to-plane expansion mixes polarizations y y Duplicate of open PR #17 (2025-08-12), which adds the missing polarization match. There is no issue for it.
(not drafted) Multi-direction parity SMatrices.interface IndexError n n Fixed upstream in 4b06735 (2024-11-21), released in 0.4.6. It still fails on 0.4.5.
(not drafted) Skew-cell orders, evanescent cylindrical widths, chiral sphere parity – – Already reported as #14, #20 and #27, all still open.

Dropped findings:

  • Parity interface: no longer reproduces on 0.4.7 or main (fixed in 4b06735).
  • Plane-to-plane expansion: still reproduces, but open PR #17 already fixes it.
  • The six items you excluded (pole regularization, degree-6 EBCM floor, SciPy subnormal Hankel, companion notebook, thermal radiation, G/F normalization) were not drafted.
  • A search of all 8 upstream issues and 29 PRs found no other duplicates.

How some findings were split or grouped:

  • The direct-sum finding became two issues (07 and 08) because the two bugs are in separate code paths.
  • "HDF5 origins and local-mode indices" is one issue (11). Its origin loss comes from SphericalWaveBasis._from_iterable being a classmethod, so every set operation on a basis drops the positions. The same pattern causes the alignment loss in 15.
  • 14 and 18 are both in pw.to_sw, and 16 and 17 share the same cos θ → sin θ rebuilding pattern. You may want to merge either pair.

Things I'm unsure about:

  • 12: chirality_density has no docstring. I verified the growth with interval length, the NaN and the zero-width problem. The point about the up/down interference phase is marked as tentative in the draft.
  • 14: I replaced your finding's wave vector (0.2+1j, …) with a passive metal-like example. The original implies a gain medium (Im ε < 0) and mixes in a second failure, where sqrt(k·k) has the opposite sign of the material wave number. I left that second failure out of the draft.
  • 06: real but low impact, since it only shows up for |kpar| of about 1e-60 and below.
  • 19: the draft says I didn't isolate which partial sum loses the accuracy.
  • 09 and 11: I didn't check which dataset names the tmat.h5 standard specifies. The drafts only state that the writer and the reader disagree.
  • Proposed fixes: I verified the fixes suggested in 02, 10 and 13, and the root cause of 14, by patching locally. The other suggested fixes are unverified proposals.

Also noticed, not drafted: numpy 2.5 emits "'where' used without 'out'" UserWarnings from sw.rotate, sw.translate and pw.translate. They look harmless because the masked entries are zeroed afterwards. SMatrices.cd also raises TypeError when given a plain list.

I replaced local paths in the .out files with .../site-packages/ and bare script names. Otherwise they are the raw captures. The .md output blocks are trimmed to the relevant lines, and I checked all drafts for terms you didn't want mentioned.
